sources.title: Project Management Professional (PMP) Examination Content Outline - July 2026
sources.authority: Controls the examination domains, task coverage, eligibility paths, training-hour requirements, examination format, question types, breaks, retake policy, and continuing-certification summary.
sources.limitations: The outline does not disclose confidential exam questions and is not a complete textbook for every project-management practice tested.

sources.title: Project Management Professional (PMP) Certification
sources.authority: Current public summary of education, experience, training, application, and exam-day requirements.
sources.limitations: The webpage may change; learners must verify current requirements directly with PMI before applying.

sources.title: What's New in the Updated PMP Exam
sources.authority: Official public explanation of the July 2026 changes, future-focused content, domain-weight changes, and planned late-Q4 2026 live-training eligibility changes.
sources.limitations: PMI has stated that the exact late-Q4 2026 training-change start date will be announced separately.

sources.title: PMI Ethics Guidelines and Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
sources.authority: Defines the ethical values and conduct expectations applicable to PMI members, certification holders, volunteers, and certification applicants.
sources.limitations: The course provides educational interpretation only; PMI controls the code and ethics-enforcement process.

sources.title: A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK Guide) - Eighth Edition
sources.authority: Provides current PMI principles, performance domains, technical content, and ways-of-working guidance used as a principal reference for project practice.
sources.limitations: The PMP exam is not written from one book alone. Learners must use legally acquired copies, and the course must paraphrase copyrighted material unless licensed.

sources.title: GAO Schedule Assessment Guide: Best Practices for Project Schedules
sources.authority: Documents ten best practices for developing and maintaining reliable, high-quality schedules and explains the role of integrated schedules in risk and change analysis.
sources.limitations: A federal audit guide is not identical to PMI examination content; it is used as an authoritative practical example and comparison source.

sources.owner: United States Department of Justice Office of the Inspector General
sources.title: The FBI's Pre-Acquisition Planning for and Controls Over the Sentinel Case Management System
sources.jurisdiction: United States federal information technology acquisition
sources.authority: Documents the terminated Virtual Case File effort and identified weaknesses involving requirements, investment management, management continuity, oversight, integration, and scheduling.
sources.limitations: The case is historical and context-specific. It illustrates governance and delivery risks but does not prove that one methodology guarantees success.

sources.title: NASA Major Projects: Portfolio Is at Risk for Continued Cost Growth and Schedule Delays
sources.authority: Reports cost and schedule deterioration across NASA major projects and discusses technical issues, risky management decisions, aggressive schedules, reserve levels, and integration-and-test risk.
sources.limitations: Portfolio observations are historical and must not be generalized without considering mission complexity, technical uncertainty, and project context.

sources.title: Cost Estimate of the James Webb Space Telescope - NASA Lessons Learned Information System
sources.authority: Describes Joint Confidence Level cost-and-schedule analysis, Monte Carlo treatment of risk-register inputs, documentation needs, training needs, and independent review considerations.
sources.limitations: The lesson explains one NASA methodology and does not require every organization to use the same quantitative model.

sources.title: Federal Real Property: GSA Could Better Identify Risks of Unforeseen Conditions in Repair and Alteration Projects
sources.authority: Provides empirical findings from 18 projects, including the frequency and cost or schedule effects of unforeseen conditions and gaps between risk identification and actual project experience.
sources.limitations: The sample is limited to the reviewed GSA repair and alteration projects and is not a universal construction benchmark.

sources.title: The Cancellation of the Benefits Payment Card Project
sources.jurisdiction: United Kingdom public-sector information technology and commercial delivery
sources.authority: Documents major financial loss and project-management lessons involving risk, commercial structure, dependencies, delivery assumptions, and governance in a large technology-enabled change program.
sources.limitations: The case is historical, national-context specific, and should be used to teach analysis rather than assign simplistic single-cause blame.
